messages.subject: Beamer to Markdown conversion?
parts:
I have some .Rnw files using the beamer document class that I would like to translate into an .Rpres file.

There is enough regularity in the LaTeX markup that I with some playing around using emacs keyboard macros, sed scripts and pandoc I could do most of the translation but that sort of stuff was much more fun when I was young and would do it just to see if I could.

Before embarking on this, has anyone been here before me and can provide recommendations on tools to do this?  In particular, is there an easy way of taking a file and converting

<<foo,option1=val,option2=val>>=
... R code
@

to 

```{r foo,option1=val,option2=val}
--- R code
```

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Beamer to Markdown conversion?
parts:
In theory, you can just use <<>>= for R Markdown. The knitr document
parser and renderer are independent, i.e. you can use the Rnw parser,
but with the Rmd renderer. For example,

library(knitr)
pat_rnw()
render_markdown()
out = knit(text = '<<foo,tidy=FALSE>>=
1+1
@'
)
cat(out)

You will get Markdown output:

```r
1+1
```

```
## [1] 2
```

This is probably not well-known to most knitr users, and I have rarely
mentioned it in the public. Although this is possible, I do not want
to have a mixture of syntax in mind, so you are still recommended to
make the conversion. Below is the code that I wrote in two minutes and
was not tested:

library(knitr)
x = readLines('foo.Rnw')
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$chunk.begin, '```{r \\1}', x)
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$chunk.end, '```', x)
x = gsub(all_patterns$rnw$inline.code, '`r \\1`', x)
writeLines(x, 'foo.Rmd')

Converting other LaTeX commands to Markdown should be easy with
Pandoc, but I guess the pain is that Rnw is not LaTeX, and I'm not
sure what Pandoc is going to do with the R code chunks when converting
the Rnw document to Markdown.

Regards,
Yihui
